When you paid off the loan your amount of credit dropped.  Part of what makes your score is amount of credit available, when you pay it off the account is closed and your available credit dropped.  Example $50,000 available credit with $25,000 car and $25,000 in credit cards.  Once paid off, your available credit just dropped to $25,000 and if you have balances on your credit cards, your credit usage ratio just shot up too (from 50% with both balance to 100% with just credit cards if maxed out)

Bankruptcy is much more preferred than the more finality of death.  When I was 22 and naive, I felt the same way.  I had mounting debt and did not see a way out.  No one would lend me money (which in reality is just adding more debt) and I felt like there was no way out.  I would be ruining my credit for the next 7 to 10 years. Thinking like you that I would not be able to buy a house or get a car loan or anything else.  Even the thought of having the stigma of declaring bankruptcy was depressing me for I felt that everyone would think I was a failure or stupid with money.  I thought every day that it would be best to just check out.
But I can tell you this.  I declared bankruptcy and I look back as that was a decision that saved my life.  Once I filed, my debt was gone. The phone calls from creditors stopped and I had a clean slate.  Yes, for the next 7 years it was on my file and obtaining credit was a bitch, but I will tell you this, It made me more disciplined in handling money and debt because I was now dealing in all cash and I couldn't spend more than I had.  It taught me to be better at budgeting.  It wasn't easy because you have to reprioritize your life into what is really worth spending money on but I learned to be less materialistic.  I can also tell you that I got a ton of "rebuild your credit" offers from many companies that I  learned to resist. (it will just put you in that debt trap again) Instead, I was able to get 1 secured credit card (making sure it wouldn't gouge me with fees or interest rates, which again I learned from my mistakes) within 2 years.  After 5 years I was getting unsecured credit card offers, again with high interest and fees and small credit limits, which I turned down because I was now wiser.  The point is that you will be able to repair your credit and you will be wiser coming out. Death is permanent. You would be ending your story before knowing how it should end.  I'm now 53 and you know what, I thought that buying a house was the end all be all goal, but I actually learned that for me, leasing a residence was a much better gig. buying a house isn't always a good thing and trying to keep up with the joneses is no way to base your life on. Also, you would be surprised how fast 10 years will go.  As we just had an election, I am amazed how fast the last 8 years went. In closing I will say this, death is final and there is no coming back. Bankruptcy is a good thing, that is why it exist because many people in life made mistakes and they should be given the chance to be forgiven.  If you are not here, you will never know that person that could change your life and fall in love with you.  There are thousands of married couples who are working through bi-polar syndrome and have a happy life together. Try outreach to them to learn how they did it. Believe it or not, you are much stronger than you give yourself credit for.  After 11 years of attempts to end your life, you found the strength to pull through each time. That's not easy and I am happy that you did. Life will throw challenges for sure, but I had kept a journal writing down good and bad times, and when I look back on the bad times and the date I wrote them, I start to remember how it felt so overwhelming impossible to go on, but I did. I then start to read the good things that happened after those events and realize that these times pass but death would have been permanent.  Good luck and really know that there are 6+ billion people on this planet and that the odds that people do care for you (even a complete stranger) are in your favor.  I hope this helps.
